title: NoSQL Families: Key-Value, Document, Wide-Column and Graph
oneLiner: Redis, MongoDB, Cassandra and Neo4j: what each family stores, how you query it, what it gives up, and how to choose.
keyTakeaway: Each NoSQL family trades something (joins, multi-row transactions, immediate consistency) for one strength: key lookups, self-contained documents, huge write volume across many nodes, or relationship traversal. Pick by access pattern, keep a relational database as the default, and use quorums (R + W > N) when replicas must agree.
explanation: NoSQL is not one thing. Key-value stores, document databases, wide-column stores and graph databases solve different problems, and choosing between them (or sticking with SQL) is a common system design interview question. This lesson shows what working with each looks like and when each is the right tool.
